chapter: Package shows, Miami and the USO
title: Boston's Tick Tock and the 1949 package show
summary: After 1948 Long Island dates he plays Boston and runs his own package show south by Greyhound.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Where do you go from Farmingdale? This is still '47.
In '48 we just played around--
But '48 is a recording band.
But I did play--this bass player, a fat guy, white--
Chubby Jackson.
We played a club of his
out on Long Island, '48--
Same group?
Yeah.
And '49.
Then we went up to Boston and went back into the Tick Tock.
Yeah.
And then from there we booked the Boston show--I had my own show there--
went all the way to Florida. I had my own Greyhound bus.
What kind of show was this, a package show?
A package show.
Singers and dancers?
Yeah.
Do you have a picture of that?
I have a picture, I can find it. I saw one not long ago.
That would be good to
I'll find one. Sam Robbins--Sam and his brother.
What were you playing, clubs or theatres?
We were playing in theatres.
Theatres, really?
Al the way down from here to Florida.
I never heard you mention anything about that before.
I didn't mention that too much.
You probably didn't do too good with it then.
We did fairly well.
